purpose: Held-out negatives with an already-damaged sofa and no chewing: does the model alert on visible damage instead of the chewing itself? Evaluated once with the test set.
how_to_use: Save clips as D01.mp4 … D05.mp4 in data/Test-Videos and label them blind with the test set; label what is visible (a clip where the dog does bite the sofa is positive).

prompts.camera: a pet camera placed low on the floor about one meter from the sofa
prompts.light: mixed warm lamp light and cool TV glow
prompts.action: lies asleep on the seat cushion right next to the existing tear, breathing slowly
prompts.prompt: Home security footage, mixed warm lamp light and cool TV glow. Recorded by a pet camera placed low on the floor about one meter from the sofa. The room is a Japanese-style room with tatami mats with a sage green slipcovered sofa. A tan short-haired chihuahua lies asleep on the seat cushion right next to the existing tear, breathing slowly. Before the clip starts the sofa is already damaged: one seat cushion has a large old tear with white stuffing poking out, and the front of the armrest is frayed with loose threads. The damage is already there at the start and does not change during the clip: the dog's mouth never bites, chews or pulls the sofa and no new tears or stuffing appear. The view is locked off for the whole clip: one continuous take, no camera motion, no zoom. Realistic animal motion, realistic lighting, no people, no on-screen text.

Setting: cluttered student apartment, dim blue dusk light from the window, with a dusty pink velvet loveseat. What happens: a Dalmatian walks past the sofa, sniffs the stuffing lying on the floor for a moment and leaves. Before the clip starts the sofa is already damaged: the skirt along the bottom is ripped and hanging, and a few tufts of old stuffing lie on the floor in front of it. The damage is already there at the start and does not change during the clip: the dog's mouth never bites, chews or pulls the sofa and no new tears or stuffing appear. Single uninterrupted shot, fixed framing, no zoom, natural dog behaviour, no humans, no text, not stylised or cinematic.
